Currently
I’m a Data Analyst at Mosscare St Vincent’s Housing Group in Manchester, and previously a Research Associate in Statistics at the University of Manchester. My interests sit at the meeting point of statistical theory and machine learning: functional data analysis, nonparametric methods, and the challenge of turning large, noisy datasets into something you can actually reason about.

title: Hello from a Quarto site
text:
Welcome to the new site. It’s built with Quarto, which means posts like this one can mix prose with live R, Python, or Julia — the same tools I use day to day.
Here’s a code block to prove the point (display-only for now):
library(ggplot2)

# kernel density estimate — the motif in the site logo
ggplot(faithful, aes(waiting)) +
  geom_density(fill = "#1E5C4A", alpha = 0.15, colour = "#1E5C4A") +
  theme_minimal()

title: About
text:
Diego Perez Ruiz
Statistician & Data Analyst

  
  
  




Thanks for stopping by. I’m a statistician and data analyst based in Manchester, working at the meeting point of statistical theory and machine learning.
My work centres on functional data and nonparametric statistics — methods for making sense of large, noisy datasets and separating the consistent patterns from the noise. I currently work as a Data Analyst at Mosscare St Vincent’s Housing Group, and previously held research posts in statistics at the University of Manchester.
You can see what I’ve been building on the Projects and Software pages, or get in touch here.
Biography
I am broadly interested in statistical theory and methodology, with a particular focus on functional data and nonparametric statistics. Statistics matters more than ever because of the ease with which we now collect large amounts of data — and the real challenge is sorting through it to separate consistent patterns from noise. How best to use the tools that let us do that is the focus of my work.
I completed my PhD in Mathematical Sciences at the University of Manchester. Before Manchester, I did an MSc in Statistics and Probability at the Center for Mathematical Research (CIMAT), and prior to that a BSc in Applied Mathematics and Computer Science at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM).

title: Predicting hypoglycaemia from CGM in CHI
text: Modelling the prediction of hypoglycaemia from continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) in congenital hyperinsulinism (CHI). Parents of children with complex diseases need clear, understandable information about the condition to improve health outcomes — a goal that shaped both the modelling and how results were communicated.

title: Probabilistic modelling of cycling-accident risk
text: Cycling is an often-overlooked mode of transport for both commuting and recreation, and one that has grown in popularity — while being environmentally friendly, economical, and healthy. This project builds probabilistic models of cycling-accident risk, using Greater Manchester as a case study.
